answer: Each identity must hold a unique optical path, or the herd is cheap to clone. A candidate posts 11.6 POA for a 7-minute slot at a seed-chosen 3-face prism, tilt hidden until start. They fire a 22-bit sparrow pulse at a sealed 40 cm mirror 8.2 m downrange; two clocks accept only a 54.0-55.4 ns echo whose RGB bins match the seed table within 1.5%. Eighty aliases would freeze 928 POA and eighty benches. Auditors recompute the tilt and confirm single occupancy. Reuse, a copied sparrow pulse, or an echo off by more than 0.8 ns burns 41% of the stake and darkens the path for four epochs.
